purpose: Compare lexical retrieval, parent-like unconstrained two-hop graph activation and candidate conservative qualified one-hop activation on current-run ClayGraph questions.

corpus.construction: Small manually assembled evidence mini-corpus from already read current branch artifacts and FRANK runtime source. Gold targets were defined from explicit source statements before candidate scoring.
corpus.independence_boundary: Gold is source-grounded, but graph edges were manually encoded from explicit interconnect/dependency relations; structural bias remains possible.

questions.query: What store is the process crossing workspace bridge read by Core into INNER_STATE?
Which architecture rule prevents active associative memory from becoming execution authority?
Which research requires incompatible alternatives and semantic topology to be preserved rather than flattened into physical storage?
What should supply bounded memory candidates to FRANK without replacing exact CognitiveFrame truth?
Why should 71 database files not map one to one to semantic organs?

result.candidate_vs_lexical: RECALL_PLUS_0.1667; PRECISION_PLUS_0.07; slightly smaller returned context; roughly 2x lexical execution time in this tiny Python environment
result.decision_effect: Supports further testing of qualified conservative expansion; does not justify promotion.

limitations: Not tools/claygraph_benchmark.py output and not a live FRANK benchmark.
Tiny corpus and five questions; metrics are unstable and non-generalizable.
Graph edges were manually encoded from explicit source relationships; candidate policy can benefit from topology choice.
Microsecond-scale Python timings are environment-specific and not meaningful for live FRANK latency.
No vector retrieval, full SQLite FTS corpus, memory-footprint or update-amplification measurement.
